 Dated this the 6th day of April, 2018
 Judgment
Vinod Chandran, J.
The petitioner, a partnership firm, dealing in edible oil and allied products, is situated in Vadakkekkad Grama panchayat in Thrissur District.
The firm is conducted on the basis of Ext.P1 licence issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The work in the establishment is done by their own skilled workers.
When the functions of the firm was going on smoothly, the respondents 5 to 7 and their henchmen made illegal demands.

In the meantime, petitioner's workers submitted applications for registration under Rule 26A as is seen from Exts.P6 to P8.
2.

At the time of admission on 07-12-2017, this Court passed an interim order directing the police to ensure that there WP(C) 39388/2017 is no obstruction caused to the loading and unloading work carried on by the petitioner with its own workers.
3. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent-Board submits that the area where the petitioner's firm situates is a Scheme covered area.

But that is of no consequence when the Navabharath Trading Company vs State Of Kerala on 7 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172466828/
3 petitioner has their own workers, registered under Rule 26A, the Writ Petition is disposed of declaring that the petitioner would be entitled to carry out the work in the firm with its own workers, who have sought registration under Rule 26A, subject to the result of the applications for registration pending before the 4 th respondent.

entities.text: Navabharath Trading Company vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 4th respondent is also directed to consider and pass orders on Exts.P6 to P8 applications as expeditiously as possible.
No costs.

Sd/-
